topic.angle: Losses feel bigger than equal gains

body.claim: Empirically, losses tend to be treated as if they were twice as large as an equivalent gain.
body.why: This is called loss aversion. In 1979, Daniel Kahneman and his associate Amos Tversky originally coined the term "loss aversion" in their initial proposal of prospect theory.

probes.question: True or false: loss aversion means a loss and an equal gain feel about the same.
Which psychologist, with Amos Tversky, coined the term loss aversion in 1979?
